items.Sentence: Rags and other large items are removed manually from the bar screen.
The headworks was designed and built with a grit chamber... The grit chamber requires manual removal of collected solids.
The headworks was designed and built with a ... solids comminutor with a parallel channel for bypass during comminutor maintenance.
Two aerated ponds provide secondary treatment of the screened sewage and are capable of operating in series or parallel... Each pond is mixed and aerated by two surface aerators...
The settling pond is a 10-foot deep clay-lined and rock armored structure that receives effluent from the two aerated ponds.
Wastewater from the transfer wet well is pumped into the Suspended Air Flotation (SAF) system.
The influent water is coagulated and flocculated in a 3,500-gallon chemical mixing tank.
The influent water is coagulated and flocculated in a 3,500-gallon chemical mixing tank.
The Permittee utilizes a Fuzzy Filter (FF) compressible media deep bed filtration system to achieve tertiary treated effluent. The filters automatically go offline and into backwash...

Following the filtration system, water flows into a 3,000-gallon tank, referred to as the “purge tank.” ... and acts as a flow equalization tank between the filters and the pasteurization disinfection system.

Treatment operations at the Facility include ... a pasteurization disinfection system... The minimum required pasteurization temperature is 162.4°F for 10 seconds, but the Permittee generally operates at 165°F.
The air is heated using the exhaust from a Capstone 30-kW microturbine, supplemented by a duct burner as needed for additional heat. The plant utilizes electricity produced by the turbine.
Following disinfection, tertiary treated wastewater flows to either of the two effluent storage ponds. The two on-site storage ponds have a combined capacity of 23.14 million gallons.
The solids dewater in bins before being transferred to the on-site compost facility.
The solids are composted using static aeration to meet or exceed title 14 standards, and the composted solids are used on site.
Biosolids generated during the treatment process accumulate in the aeration and settling ponds, where they undergo anaerobic digestion and compaction.
Solids are drained into a perforated 5-gallon bucket and deposited in a trash container for removal to a landfill by a licensed hauler.
The Permittee plans to mine sludge from the bottom of the ponds during periods of low flow and remove it through the SAF system to mitigate future sludge blanket accumulation.
Sludge that collects in the aeration and settling ponds was removed most recently in 2007.
Settling pond water can be recirculated to the headworks through Control Structure No. 1 to dilute incoming wastewater and reseed with good nitrifying bacteria.
